branches.title: Mask selection as a side channel
branches.stage: formal metric error corrected; position-channel pilot designed; zero experimental runs
branches.question: Can a content-dependent adaptive sampler encode hidden-image information through selected patch positions, and does this bias masked-image learning?
branches.novelty: CORRECTION: the earlier I(Y; M | V) proposal is identically zero when V includes spatial positions of visible patches, since M is the complement of those positions. This is a definitional problem, NOT negative empirical evidence. Informative missingness (GRU-D), adaptive token selection (AdaMAE) and adaptive masking are established. The only plausible new claim concerns mask-policy-induced shortcut learning under carefully controlled sample selection; no novelty claim yet.
branches.pilot: Define S=visible position set, B=values of visible patches without their indices, and T=(S,B) as actual encoder input. Compare position-only S probe, content-only B probe, and S+B probe on a balanced synthetic dataset engineered so visible patch values are identical across labels while the adaptive policy uses unseen context to select blank positions. Compare fixed/random masks and a selector with no access to hidden context; hold count, grid, split and compute fixed. Then test whether a public MAE checkpoint's advantage survives masking-policy swaps and held-out inputs. Report I(Y;S|B) ONLY with B explicitly excluding position indices, not the invalid I(Y;M|T). This sanity example is not evidence of publication novelty. Toy CPU; actual pretrained model small GPU if needed.
branches.stop: If the position-only control does not carry repeatable information on held-out inputs, or the shortcut has no measurable representation/downstream effect after policy controls, retire the performance-inflation claim. Review direct prior art before submitting.

branches.title: Entity linking recall under fixed candidate cost
branches.stage: INDEPENDENT MULTI-SOURCE DEVELOPMENT PILOT COMPLETE (Oct 27): Leipzig University's Music Brainz 20K public cluster-labeled synthetic data was audited and evaluated in memory with deterministic CID-disjoint fit/dev/sealed partitions. Fit-only TF-IDF weighting and frozen cosine ranking compared uniform top-K, global top-B and 16 preregistered rank-preserving randomized source-offset controls at matched budgets. This is development data only; all numerical results are kept private. The strongest global-score baseline approaches its candidate-oracle ceiling, and the large fixed-K discrepancy at tight budgets is confounded by known multi-positive query degrees. Dataset is a useful control, not a main novelty evaluation. Sealed test unexamined for retrieval outcomes. No learned allocator or full production pipeline runtime established.
branches.question: Without knowing which sources have matches at inference time, can an allocation policy learn both match-existence probability and last-positive-rank completion curves to improve complete-link retrieval among all source queries under fixed candidate count AND end-to-end wall time, versus QASP-style and progressive-ER baselines?
branches.novelty: The PACMMOD/SIGMOD 2025 Progressive ER formal objective maximizes progressive recall@N of verified PAIRS, assumes oracle pair verification and explicitly excludes verification time from reported runtime. QASP (Jul 2026) predicts recall of nearest-neighbor search as probes increase; nearest-neighbor recall is NOT recall of all semantically true entity links. The proposed completion event max_true_match_rank<=K differs from both losses, but this is not proof of novel algorithm. Distinct evaluation must include multi-positive sources (standard clean-clean datasets often assume within-source no duplicates), real full-pipeline runtime, calibrated completion prediction, and equal-budget strong baselines. Critical new gate (Oct 27): allocation over positive queries only is oracle information leakage unless positivity is inferable at inference. Estimate p_i*F_i(k) over all S1, assess null-query opportunity cost and incomplete ground truth. No new algorithm claimed. A new necessary CONTROL is randomized source-level monotone score offsets: a policy can redistribute budget across sources without changing their local candidate ranks or using any label. Neither stochastic prioritization (SPER) nor generic budgeted success curves are intrinsically novel. A learned all-link allocator must show more than what random budget concentration achieves at equal B. DATASET GATE: WDC Products EDBT 2024's official val/test subsets assign two offers per product, so its isolated test does not provide multi-positive complete-link recall; do not treat pairwise evaluation as a multi-link retrieval benchmark. Leipzig Music Brainz 20K offers CID-labeled multi-source groups but has synthetic perturbations and source-specific duplication assumptions. Novelty must generalize beyond generated duplicate examples, under sealed cluster-disjoint testing.
branches.pilot: NEXT: Audit and freeze a harder REAL-WORLD multi-positive entity dataset, with complete-link label assumptions explicitly tested. Preserve deterministic cluster-disjoint fit/calibration/test and include all zero-match queries in budget. Use Leipzig Music Brainz 20K only as a documented synthetic control: train-only IDF, frozen cosine scoring, matched candidate B, uniform, global-score, 16 predetermined source-offset seeds; add a degree-capacity upper bound showing that fixed-K cannot complete queries with more than K true links. On harder data evaluate fitted probability-of-completion versus strong global/top-B, randomized concentration, QASP/Progressive ER/SPER variants under full CPU cost and inference-available signals. Do not open the sealed Leipzig split or claim paper novelty during development.
branches.stop: If no reliable gain over strong global-score AND QASP/progressive baselines on a new sealed cluster-disjoint test, or if gain is due to incomplete annotations/model-selection leakage, retire standalone adaptive-allocation claim. Candidate-universe missing links cannot be repaired by reallocation. Also stop novel learned-allocation claim if it cannot beat an uninformed rank-preserving source-offset baseline on the prospectively sealed test. No novel algorithm inferred from artificial score perturbations. Do not interpret a single-positive-only official benchmark as evidence for multi-positive all-links completion. Stop any new-data claim if controls differ in candidate universe, annotation coverage, or information available at inference. New finding: When a simple global-score allocation already approaches candidate-oracle completion on synthetic duplicates, retire that dataset as primary method-novelty evidence and seek harder real-world independent annotations. Do not advertise the mathematically predetermined failure of K<true-link-count uniform retrieval as algorithmic discovery.

branches.title: Small formal proofs for retrieval and selection
branches.stage: elementary formulation plus verified 2-query greedy failure counterexample; no new theory paper result
branches.question: Under what realistic constraints on calibration error, fairness or retrieval costs can a complete-link global-budget allocation guarantee robust coverage?
branches.novelty: The standard deterministic all-link allocation problem reduces to choosing per-query ranks under a total budget (multiple-choice knapsack or threshold-cost selection); this alone is a known optimization structure, not an original theorem. Seek a genuine robustness or calibration result, and compare established budgeted ranking/scheduling literature. Closely related general theory already studies monotone task-success probability vs budget with censored feedback (Bachoc et al., arXiv:2508.05844, revised Feb 2026); reuse of this structure is not a new theorem.
branches.pilot: Deterministic small-instance enumerator run in this cycle: F_A(0,1,2)=(0,.40,.41); F_B=(0,0,1); total B=2. Sequential one-step marginal greedy allocates (2,0), objective .41; exhaustive exact allocation (0,2) obtains 1.00. This establishes NONCONCAVE cumulative-completion curves can defeat naive greedy, not novelty and not an empirical ER outcome. An allocator must use exact small-budget dynamic programming or a defensible approximation; validate full-runtime and calibration assumptions. Seek nontrivial theorem only after literature review.
branches.stop: If bound is vacuous under realistic distributions, retire.

policies.rule: Mandatory manuscript AI-use disclosure; authors are responsible for all claims and originality.
LLM use permitted; disclosure encouraged, reproducibility and correct citations mandatory.

LLM assistance is permitted with human responsibility. A mandatory LLM Usage Statement must disclose tools, stages, and extent, including grammar editing. Without an eligible reciprocal reviewer among coauthors, an author may appear on at most one submission; overall 25-paper author cap. OpenReview profiles and author lists must be ready by Nov 10.

Substantive LLM-generated technical content must be disclosed; editing, literature search, and code assistance alone do not require disclosure. Eight main-track submissions maximum per author; no placeholder abstract; potential ACM open-access APC.

AI writing assistance does not require disclosure under venue policy; AI-assisted research does require careful disclosure. Authors must make substantial intellectual contributions and remain accountable. Research-quality, anonymity and ACM OA/APC constraints apply.
policies.flag: AI research disclosure; author contribution and APC check

policies.rule: Mandatory AI Usage Disclosure after references for ALL submissions: disclose ideation, literature, experimental design, code, data, writing, tools and extent. Solely LLM-generated paper content is prohibited outside illustrative/experimental uses. Generalized harmonic author quota: max 2 papers if all single-author, max 20 if all 10-author; other mixes vary; desk rejection for violations.
policies.flag: mandatory end-to-end AI disclosure; prohibit AI-only manuscripts; harmonic per-author submission quota

policies.rule: Unlike FAccT 2026, substantive AI-generated content is allowed with full author responsibility and mandatory generative-AI usage statement in anonymous endmatter; disclose research ideation, analysis, methods and generated writing and human review. Human authors alone assume responsibility; no AI author.
policies.flag: mandatory generative AI usage statement; 2027 reverses 2026 text-generation ban

policies.rule: IEEE disclosure of AI-generated article content identifying tool, sections and extent; basic grammar editing exempt but disclosure recommended. In-person presentation mandatory; first-author max two submissions; archival full paper restricted to four technical pages, fifth nontechnical page costs USD 200.
policies.flag: IEEE substantive content disclosure; physical attendance; first-author <=2

policies.rule: MIDL 2027 official policy: LLM use is limited to language/formatting edits. LLM-generated research ideas, study designs, analyses, results, and substantive content are prohibited; this autonomous research workflow is not eligible for a MIDL 2027 paper.
policies.flag: restrictive: no AI-generated research idea, experiment, analysis, or substantive writing

policies.rule: Authors must disclose and motivate generative AI use in HotCRP's Generative AI usage considerations field when registering, including research methodology and paper preparation. Any AI-generated idea must be independently developed and validated by authors. Complete author list with ORCID and COIs is fixed at Nov 10 abstract registration; max 6 submissions per author per cycle; artifacts must remain anonymized.
policies.flag: mandatory AI-use rationale and disclosure; independent validation; fixed Nov 10 abstract; cap 6

policies.rule: ACM/PLDI: material AI use in scientific research design, methods, code, experiment and analysis must be described in detail in the methods; writing-only AI assistance need not be disclosed under updated ACM policy. False citations/results are desk-rejectable; 2027 Data-Availability Statement required before references.
policies.flag: disclose research-stage AI; writing-only exempt; data availability statement

policies.rule: Oct 31, 2026 AoE; six-page independent submission (not ARR), double-blind, real-world deployed/expected-to-deploy NLP or speech system, mandatory Limitations, no non-anonymized code link. Completely AI-generated papers, hallucinated references and thinly sliced overlapping submissions risk desk rejection and sanctions. Writing assistants permitted under ACL policy but authors remain responsible.
policies.flag: requires deployed system and substantive human research; disallow fully AI-made papers or sliced duplicates

examples.title: Robin: multi-agent system for scientific discovery
examples.note: Iterative hypothesis/analysis loop with experiments performed by humans; not a fully autonomous wet lab.

examples.title: What-If World: causal physical-intervention benchmark (2026)
examples.note: Explicitly leaves empirical downstream-planner utility untested; CC-10 must still separate itself from related planner/control studies.

examples.note: Executing agent-written analysis does not guarantee the intended numerical quantity is recovered.

examples.title: GRU-D and informative missingness (2018)
examples.note: The pattern of missingness can itself predict the target; generic mask-side-channel novelty is blocked.

examples.title: AI Agent Swarms as Researchers (Gusev & Bernal Neira, Sep 2026)
examples.kind: Published arXiv preprint with publicly released unedited AI-agent research corpus
examples.note: Broad human task prompts led to many draft manuscripts, notes, agent reviews and some Lean proofs. Authors do NOT claim these drafts are accepted papers or fully independently verified; tag paper-v1 captures original untouched snapshot.

examples.title: Pinned agent-swarm paper-v1 inventory metadata audit (Oct 27 2026)
examples.kind: Direct GitHub source inspection; inventory counts only
examples.note: 53 listed IDs, of which 45 are paper candidates and 8 proposed catalysis experiments. 22 full paper documents, 9 summaries, 18 notes-only, 4 program documents. Lean status self-reported: 5 Done, 13 Partial, 9 Possible, 26 Not applicable. No Lean kernel checks, scientific replications, or peer review verified.

examples.title: Cross-Modal Semantic Alignment Via Ensemble Audio-Text Features for XACLE Challenge (ICASSP 2026)
examples.kind: Accepted, published two-page challenge system paper (rank 2)
examples.note: Ensembles of CLAP-family, Whisper and text encoder features combined through regressors already exist. A generic multi-encoder regressor is not a novel XACLE 2027 contribution.

examples.title: The TMU System for the XACLE Challenge: Training Large Audio Language Models with CLAP Pseudo-Labels (ICASSP 2026)
examples.note: Published rank-3 challenge result reported SRCC 0.632 vs baseline 0.334. Its code is open. Seen-generator setting differs from 2027 challenge unseen-generator shift.

examples.title: CC-08 source-certificate audit, Oct 27 (M1 and M3)
examples.kind: Direct public artifact inspection plus limited independent exact arithmetic
examples.note: M1 four printed examples re-evaluated with exact rational arithmetic (4/4 matched stated formulas); M3 public experimental count arithmetic matches 289. README records historical fingerprint drift, and M3 record explicitly lacks whole-project kernel replay. No Lean build, empirical validation, or manuscript-priority check was performed.

examples.title: SPO-CLAPScore: Standardized Preference Optimization for Audio–Text Alignment (2026 XACLE)
examples.kind: Published public system report and released code (rank 6, no claim of 2027 success)
examples.note: Reported 2026 test SRCC 0.6142; already learns human listener preferences with standardized scores. A shallow ranking/calibration head alone is not a novel 2027 generator-generalization paper. Its seen-generator setting differs from the unseen-generator 2027 challenge.

examples.title: FIRE-Bench (ICML 2026)
examples.note: Agents rediscover known, verifiable ML findings given only high-level questions. Generic full-cycle rediscovery benchmarks already exist.

examples.title: Artisan / Automated Table Reproduction via Code Generation (ASE 2026)
examples.note: Authors report 44/60 runnable reproductions and 20 discovered errors. A generic executable paper-reproduction agent is not a new CC08 method.

examples.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery (16 Oct 2026)
examples.note: Authors report claim-level SEER medical research reproduction (2,190 atomic claims) and alternative analytical robustness tests. Overlaps CC08 generic atomic-claim replay.

examples.title: CC08 prior-art and formal-source trust-boundary audit (27 Oct 2026)
examples.kind: Public-safe source inventory plus literature review; not independent proof checking
examples.note: Reviewed FIRE-Bench, Artisan, SEER-Repro; inspected 41+7 pinned Lean modules by directory listing, root imports and verification source. No Lean compilation, all-proof scan, or scientific correctness verified.

examples.title: Beyond Compilation: evaluating faithful statement autoformalization (2026)
examples.kind: Research preprint (NeurIPS 2026 workshop acceptance reported by associated code repository)
examples.note: Shows that Lean type-checking and faithful translation of a natural-language theorem are distinct and measures this gap. CC08 cannot claim semantic-fidelity auditing itself as novel.

examples.title: When2Speak: learning when an agent should speak (2026)
examples.note: Already studies speaking versus silence in multi-party text conversations; not equivalent to HEARTBEAT causal streaming-audio timing, but prevents a generic novelty claim.

examples.title: CC08 prospective entry sample and source-audit protocol (27 Oct 2026)
examples.kind: Predeclared 12 research-entry pilot; no independent theorem verification
examples.note: Fixed 12-entry SHA256-stratified sample, identified first selected M2 public source/package scope and upstream historical-hash caveat. No compilation or corpus-level accuracy measured.

examples.title: ScientistOne: chain-of-evidence and CoE Audit for automated research (May 2026)
examples.kind: Research preprint; not verified accepted main-track paper
examples.note: Proposes evidence tracing across agent-produced research and checks score, references, specifications, and method-code alignment. Prior art against generic CC08 verification-chain claims; reported success rates belong to its authors.

examples.title: From Fluent to Verifiable: claim-level auditability and review effort (Feb 2026)
examples.note: Introduces audit-effort, evidence provenance coverage and soundness criteria for deep-research agents. Prior art against CC08 treating audit effort or claim-evidence tracing as a new objective.

examples.title: Online Budget Allocation with Censored Semi-Bandit Feedback (Bachoc et al.)
examples.note: General monotone success-probability budget curves and regret under censored semi-bandit feedback. Prior art against claiming a generic adaptive success-budget optimization formulation as an original CC11 theory contribution.

examples.title: WDC Products (EDBT 2024): test-split multi-positive limit
examples.note: The official val/test construction assigns only two offers per product. An isolated test pair cannot establish added value for retrieving every match when one entity has multiple matching offers.

examples.title: Leipzig Music Brainz 20K five-source entity-resolution corpus
examples.note: Five duplicate-free data sources with CID cluster identifiers permit a CPU-first multi-positive and null-query retrieval protocol. Records are generated corruptions; use CID-disjoint fit/dev/sealed evaluation, and validate later on independent real-world ER.

lastLiteratureAudit: 2026-10-27: WDC Products EDBT 2024 official val/test has two offers per product; Leipzig Music Brainz 20K offers five synthetic duplicate-free sources with cluster IDs. A preregistered Leipzig development-only CPU pilot verified the need for degree-aware structural controls and strong global-score baselines; it did not show new algorithm novelty and was not a final sealed benchmark. CHIIR, MLSys, ISCA/CVPR and venue-specific AI policies continue in deadlines/policies. No submission.
